A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same OptFPRL research work, including complete Appendices A–F. All 26 pages are readable, and text and rendered-page comparisons support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original numerical experiments in Appendix F. Figure 2 presents average dynamic regret for OptFPRL, FTRL, and OMD across six synthetic nonstationary scenarios.

after.justification: v3 retains the original numerical experiments in Appendix F and all six panels of Figure 2 comparing OptFPRL, FTRL, and OMD.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, prediction handling, the pruning rule, and the four regularization strategies in Section 3 are unchanged, as are the method details in Appendix A.

E1.justification: Appendix F retains the same six synthetic linear-cost scenarios, covering changes in cost direction, magnitude, switching frequency, and prediction quality. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: The same adaptive FTRL and OMD baselines participate in the corresponding Appendix F comparisons, including their optimistic variants in Scenario 6. No comparator is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: Appendix F retains the reported 16-dimensional radius-2 domain, T=5000 setup, cost schedules, tuning choices, prediction construction, and average dynamic regret metric. The testing procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The same analyses of switching frequency, varying cost magnitudes, and prediction quality remain in Appendix F, including the adverse Scenario 5. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 2 reports regret averaged over time, with the same absence of statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All six Figure 2 panels are visually identical, and their accompanying findings are unchanged, including OptFPRL's higher regret in Scenario 5. No numerical or qualitative result is added or corrected.

T1.justification: Settings 1, Theorems 3.1–3.4, the Section 4 lemmas, and the mathematical definitions and proofs in Appendices A–D are unchanged.

C1.justification: The optimistic dynamic regret guarantees and pruning contributions are retained. Changing 'greedy' to 'lazy' in the abstract aligns its terminology with the lazy-to-agile spectrum already claimed in v2's conclusion; it introduces no new contribution.

C2.justification: The state-growth explanation and applicability qualifications are unchanged. Appendix F retains the parameter-tuning explanation for OMD–OptFPRL differences and the agility-versus-stability interpretation of Scenario 5.

D1.justification: The algorithm details, numerical setup, and experiment-reproduction instructions are identical. The implementation repository reference and its embedded link target are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix E's comparison with the literature, and the bibliography are unchanged. No cited work or substantive positioning relative to prior research changes.

P1.justification: The abstract changes 'greedy and agile updates' to 'lazy and agile updates'. Section 1.2 replaces the comma after 'cone N_X(x_t)' with a period, and the arXiv version/date stamp updates. Document structure is unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 and Algorithm 1 retain their graphics, captions, legends, and positions. Page arrangement is unchanged; the copyedits cause only incidental text reflow.

improvement.justification: The abstract correction brings its terminology into agreement with the lazy-to-agile spectrum already explicit in v2's conclusion, and one punctuation error is fixed. These provide slight editorial polish without materially changing overall quality; the substantive exposition, proofs, numerical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
